assets.name: lecture_05_figure_01.png
assets.rationale: Shows the stretched segment and completed Hooke-law potential at the opening scale argument.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the potential energy that's in a string
assets.caption_hint: Hooke-law model for a stretched segment

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: Shows the board transition from mass squared proportional to length squared to rest mass proportional to length.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: energy is equal to a tension times the length

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: Records the natural-unit convention and inverse-length character of energy while the oscillator scale is discussed.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: h bar equals one and c equals one

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: Shows the dimensions of c and hbar used to construct universal units.

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: Shows the dimensions of Newton's constant inferred from gravitational acceleration.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: acceleration is G M over r squared

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: Shows the completed dimensional construction of Planck area and Planck length.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: G h bar over c cubed

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: Records the lecture's order-of-magnitude values for Planck length, time, and mass in one unobstructed board state.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Planck mass is about ten to the minus eight kilograms

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: Shows the schematic extrapolation of gauge couplings toward a high unification scale before gravity becomes strong.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: these three coupling constants come together

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_09.png
assets.rationale: Places electromagnetic and gravitational inverse-square forces side by side to identify a dimensionless gravitational strength.

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_10.png
assets.rationale: Revisits the Planck length and mass formulas at the conclusion of the localization and collapse argument.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the Planck mass and the Planck length

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_11.png
assets.rationale: Shows the formal half-sum of positive oscillator frequencies that supplies the open-string vacuum intercept.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: one half plus two halves plus three halves

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_12.png
assets.rationale: Shows the large-longitudinal-momentum expansion separating overall motion from the invariant mass term.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: E is P plus m squared over two P

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_13.png
assets.rationale: Shows the finite internal mass contribution beside the large state-independent longitudinal energy.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: subtract the momentum from the energy
assets.caption_hint: Invariant mass after subtracting overall motion

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_14.png
assets.rationale: Shows exponential damping applied term by term to the divergent sum of positive integers.

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_15.png
assets.rationale: Shows the derivative with respect to epsilon that brings down the oscillator index.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the derivative with respect to epsilon
assets.caption_hint: Derivative trick for the regulated sum

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_16.png
assets.rationale: Shows the geometric series in closed form before its small-cutoff expansion.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: the sum of a geometric series
assets.caption_hint: Closed form of the regulated geometric series

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_17.png
assets.rationale: Shows the numerator and denominator expansions used during the in-class sign checks.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: expand both the numerator and denominator

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_18.png
assets.rationale: Shows the divergent inverse-square term and finite minus-one-twelfth remainder after differentiation.
assets.caption_hint: Divergent and finite parts of the regulated sum

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_19.png
assets.rationale: Shows the restored factor of one-half and the finite minus-one-twenty-four contribution per transverse coordinate.
